articles.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
articles.summary: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
body: Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whomever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.

“So much has been written about the contents of the record —the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of “Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly,” said in an interview.
points: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.

articles.title: Does GTA VI live up to the hype? Our games editor has played it – ask her anything
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI, the biggest games release of the decade, is nearly here. Our games editor Keza MacDonald will be online from 4pm to answer all your questions. Ask a question: log in or sign up here.
body: After more than a decade and a reported billion dollars in the making, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally released on Friday. It’s one of the most anticipated games of all time.

The Guardian’s games editor, Keza MacDonald, is one of the first people in the world to have played it. Last month she visited Rockstar North’s headquarters in Edinburgh to go behind the scenes, and she’s now been playing a review copy.

So does it live up to the hype? What’s it like to play as Lucia and Jason, the series’ first double act of protagonists? How big is the new Vice City, and does it really feel alive? And are the radio stations as good as ever?
Keza will be here at 4pm today to answer your questions about the graphics, the open world, the characters, the story and anything else you want to know before you play, without spoilers.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived
articles.summary: More than a decade after Grand Theft Auto V was first released, its sequel is finally launching. On November 19th, GTA VI will be available on both the PS5 and Xbox Series X / S, and it’s quite possibly the most anticipated video game launch of all time.
body: Part of this has to do with the success of its predecessor, as GTA V sold more than 230 million copies over the last 13 years. Some of it has to do with the sheer length of time between releases, a period that was plagued by leaks and a handful of delays that made the wait even harder for fans.

But GTA VI is now a real thing you can play, and you can also keep track of all of the important post-launch information right here. That includes our own review and interviews with the development team, as well as news on just how the game ends up resonating with players.

Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just the biggest GTA game to date; it’s also the most romantic. Though the series is well known for its sordid assortment of criminal leads, GTA VI switches things up by starring a pair of thieves who also happen to fall in love after meeting while stealing a car. It’s still an open-world action game full of chaos and mayhem. But many players will also be attempting to nurture the budding relationship in between heists. The sprawling game is designed to support both audiences.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI: The Ars Technica review
articles.summary: Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner.
body: This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.

The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.

But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.

articles.title: Elton John backs Australian artists in fight against AI in surprise Aria awards appearance
articles.summary: British musician backs Not AI’s To Take campaign, saying Albanese government has ‘a duty to protect Australian artists and their work’ Aria awards 2026 red carpet: Tame Impala, Baker Boy, G Flip and more – in pictures.
body: Elton John has made a surprise appearance at the 2026 Aria awards to draw attention to Not AI’s To Take, a major campaign backed by the creative and media industries calling on the Australian government to protect copyright law in the face of lobbying from AI companies.

Delivering a pre-recorded message at Australian music’s biggest night on Wednesday, the British singer backed the new campaign, which is calling on the Albanese government to ensure Australian artists are reimbursed and consulted by AI companies interested in using their works for AI training.

“I have long admired the talent and creativity of Australian artists,” John said. “So I want to send an important message to the Australian government. You have a duty to protect Australian artists and their work. Don’t let AI use any Australian artist’s work without full permission. Please, protect the next generation of Australian artists. Thank you.”

Australian musicians Jack River, Dobby, Josh Pyke and KLP also addressed the room at Sydney’s Hordern Pavilion on behalf of Not AI’s To Take, joining the likes of Jimmy Barnes, Paul Kelly and Peter Garrett who were among the artists who launched the campaign this week.

articles.title: £10m ‘once-in-a-generation’ study to explore effects of children’s social media ban
articles.summary: Research to look at whether ban can make meaningful change in mental health and wellbeing for under-16s. Countries around the world are considering social media bans for children, but whether this would work in practice has been hotly debated.
body: Ten research projects will explore topics ranging from children’s mental health to their sleep and physical activity, comparing factors before and after the social media ban for children under 16 is introduced in the UK in spring 2027.

Backed by £9.3m of funding from Wellcome and working with more than 300,000 young people across Britain, researchers hope to provide crucial answers for those working on online safety and digital policy.

“We all know there has been a quite heated debate around the social media ban here in the UK [and] also around the world, but there is very limited scientific evidence about how social media and its restrictions [are] actually affecting the mental health of young people,” said Dr Camilla Iannone, research lead at Wellcome.
Iannone said restrictions will offer a once-in-a-generation opportunity to study at scale how social media affects young people’s mental health.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe is now one light-day away
articles.summary: After traveling through the void of space for 49 years, Voyager 1 has hit a momentous milestone: the spacecraft is now officially one light-day away from Earth, which is, as NASA put it, "very, very far." The probe crossed the milepost on Wednesday at 5:16AM ET, and is now 16.094 billion miles away…
body: It’s taken Voyager 1 almost 50 years to journey further from Earth than light can travel in 24 hours.

It’s the furthest that any human-made object has ever traveled, and Voyager 1’s journey isn’t over yet. It’s been heading towards a star called Gliese 445 in the Ursa Minor constellation since completing its primary objectives to conduct flybys of Jupiter and Saturn in 1980. That star is 17 light-years away, meaning Voyager 1 won’t pass by it for around 40,000 years, despite traveling at nearly 38,000 miles per hour.

The light-day milestone is a remarkable feat alone, but especially so when you consider that Voyager 1 is still operational. NASA has done well to keep it functioning, and it can continue to send back readings on plasma waves, magnetic fields, and space-bound particles, though it now takes radio signals an entire day to travel between Earth and the spacecraft. Voyager 2, which launched 16 days before its twin, is also expected to reach a distance of one light-day away from Earth, but not until 2035.

articles.title: Suno now lets you make AI videos for your AI music
articles.summary: Suno has introduced image and video generation in its latest effort to expand beyond being an AI music platform. The new feature, called "Visuals," allows users to turn Suno songs into AI-generated video clips that automatically lipsync to lyrics, or make images via prompt descriptions that can be…
body: The new Visuals feature generates images and 15-second videos that automatically sync with Suno songs.

Visuals is available on web, iOS, and Android. The exact layout differs across Suno’s desktop and mobile interfaces, but users will find a new Visuals tab under Create mode on each version. Web users can also access Visuals by selecting the three dot menu on a song in their library. From there, users can select which section of the track to use, up to a maximum of 15 seconds, and select a reference image to build the generated video clip.

There are three options available for the starting image reference: selecting one of the original character presets provided by Suno, uploading your own photo or artwork, or generating the image directly on Suno using descriptive prompts. The image generation capabilities also allow users to select specific aspect ratios, optimizing results for landscape or portrait modes and online platforms.

articles.title: Voyager 1 Beat the Odds and Is Still Working a Light-Day Away From Earth
articles.summary: The spacecraft stores data on an eight-track tape, but it’s managed to stay in contact with scientists for decades. Now, it’s the first human-made object to travel a light-day away from Earth.
body: One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.

Voyager 1, launched in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, is poised to achieve a historic milestone on Wednesday: It will be the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft will be so far away, that by the time its light reaches Earth, it will come from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on, and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.

“It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”

body: Like most compelling crime fiction, Jason and Lucia’s story involves an escalating series of messy events that pull them further and further from where they started, and have you constantly wondering how on earth they’re going to get out of the newest trouble they’re in. To avoid spoilers, substantive discussion of this story can only happen in the coming weeks. But I will say that I was rooting so hard for Jason and Lucia by the end that I felt quite sick with worry about what was going to happen to them, pacing back and forth in front of my TV throughout the final missions. Among all the expectations I had for GTA VI, I did not expect it to make me so emotional.

articles.title: Exclusive: Germ DM Is a Signal Alternative That’s Now on Android
articles.summary: Germ DM is an encrypted messaging platform that uses “burner cards” instead of phone numbers or usernames to compartmentalize your conversations.
body: Tessa Brown is visibly excited to talk to me about Germ DM, her secure messaging platform. It’s now available on Android, a major expansion for the small startup. Her eyes light up as she explains how her ambitious, three-person team—including an ex-Apple engineer who worked on iMessage —could pull off this platform expansion.

“It's essential to be able to talk to everybody, and that's really what this Android launch unlocks for us,” she says. Brown was previously a lecturer at Stanford University, and her cofounder, Mark Xue, worked on iMessage’s privacy provisions. The duo first launched the iOS app for Germ in 2023.

The platform expansion makes it easier to recommend Germ as an interesting alternative to Signal, especially for early adopters curious about trying new ways to message others and connect with the world.

articles.title: House Democrats Are Officially Coming for Trump’s Orbit
articles.summary: The incoming head of the House Oversight Committee sent record preservation requests to Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, JD Vance, Stephen Miller, and other administration officials.
body: Donald Trump Jr. was barefoot and beaming when a photographer snapped a group picture of him, his new bride, and his 30-or-so wedding party guests on a private island in the Bahamas last May. But that party—which was reportedly paid for by a Russian oligarch —has since turned into a legal and political headache.

In a letter sent Wednesday, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee has directed the president’s son to preserve all records related to his “lavish wedding celebrations” and his many business ventures, too.

That demand is a key step in any serious Congressional probe, and one sign among many that Democratic investigators are going after the president’s family in the new term following their massive wins in the election earlier this month.

articles.title: Security flaw found in Java, world's third-largest programming language
articles.summary: The same tech start-up that discovered a PHP flaw used AI to uncover a critical software bug in one of the world's most popular computer language programs.
body: A cyber-security firm has used artificial intelligence (AI) to uncover a critical flaw in the hugely popular computer programming language Java.
Tech start-up Calif - which recently identified a cyber-security flaw in another language, PHP - found the bug in Java's memory functions.
Java is a popular programming language used by nearly all of the world's top companies such as Apple and Amazon, as well as many banks, hospitals and governments.
It is meant to make the IT world more secure by managing your memory online, said computer scientist Professor Toby Walsh, which is why "this is such an unlikely and serious flaw".

articles.title: Lovable Wants You to Vibe Code Your Dream Job
articles.summary: This Swedish startup dominated the vibe-coded app boom. Two years after launch, Lovable is shifting gears to help users run vibe-coded businesses.
body: I squint my eyes in confusion when Anton Osika asks if I like cakes. The CEO of Lovable was in the middle of explaining how his AI startup, flush with investment cash and recently valued at over $13 billion, is ready to shift its focus after two years. Why does the vibe-coding king care if I like sweet treats? He thinks that if I do, I might be able to vibe code a living out of that.

The generative AI revolution completely flipped coding. Rather than a niche skill set where humans had to learn how to talk like computers, software development could be done by computers generating code in response to natural-language requests from humans.

Osika was early to this shift, launching a viral open-source tool in 2023, a precursor to Lovable. His mission? “Reduce barriers to build.” That initial spark ignited what is now one of Europe’s most dynamic startups.
